facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a negative governance view is that creditors now hold stronger protections: the credit facility requires disposal proceeds to repay debt, caps manager fees, and lenders waived earlier defaults, while reporting is current and the management agreement is cheaper from 2027. A clean internal-control opinion for 2026, evidence that overpaid fees are fully recouped and board detail from the proxy statement would move the view toward a lower governance risk, while a new restatement, a covenant breach at the holding company or fee payments ahead of debt reduction would move it the other way. - The 2026 proxy statement, which carries board composition, executive pay and beneficial ownership, is not in the sources, so governance and ownership conclusions are bounded to what the annual and quarterly reports state. Severity: Material. Action: supply the proxy statement. - The management agreement, trust agreement and operating agreement are not in the sources, so fee mechanics, profit allocation and creditor consent rights are known only from summaries. Severity: Material. Action: supply the executed agreements. - Restricted-payment and investment basket capacity cannot be read because the credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the room for equity leakage is not established. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the executed debt documents. - Customer concentration is stated for two of eight subsidiaries only. Severity: Low. Action: obtain customer data for the other subsidiaries. - Listing status after the 2026-01-02 exchange notice is not stated in the later filings. Severity: Low. Action: obtain an exchange notice or later filing.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The 12 supplied documents support a credit snapshot as of 2026-11-18 with limitations: the original 2024 annual report is superseded by a restatement, and no executed debt documents, ratings or market prices were supplied, so covenant conclusions rest on issuer summaries.

Current-period evidence is the strongest part of the set: the third-quarter 2026 quarterly report and earnings release, dated 14 days before the cutoff, give full statements, the debt note with its covenant test and the liquidity disclosure, and the totals checked agree with the 2025 annual report and the third-quarter 2025 report.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 7–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 27–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 94–99; EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C10
### Key findings

- The issuer is the operating company beneath a listed trust and files jointly with it. The trust only owns the company, so the consolidated statements printed under the trust's name are the issuer's consolidated statements. No company-only statements, parent-only schedule or subsidiary guarantor information were found, and the senior notes are described as unsecured obligations not guaranteed by subsidiaries.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation C12

- The original 2024 annual report is not a safe source for 2024 values. It printed net revenues of USD 2,198.23 million and total assets of USD 4,052.42 million, against USD 1,788.01 million and USD 3,297.42 million in the restated comparatives of the 2025 annual report, so every 2024 value should come from the restated comparatives.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 226–227; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 225–226; calculation C3; calculation C4

- The 2025 annual report carries an unqualified opinion on the financial statements and an adverse opinion on internal control, and management states that the control weaknesses were not fully remediated at the end of the third quarter of 2026, so the figures are usable but carry elevated reporting risk.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 221–223; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 112

- Quarterly headline lines for 2024 and 2025 (revenues, gross profit, operating income and net loss) are printed in the unaudited quarterly note of the 2025 annual report, and the fourth quarter of 2025 agrees with the full year less the nine months; first-half 2025 cash flows, balance sheets and segment detail are not available on their own because the first- and second-quarter 2025 reports and any fourth-quarter release are not in the set.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 315–316; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 226; 10-Q_2025-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C14

- Debt amounts can be read from the debt note by instrument, and management's headline debt figure is the principal, not the balance-sheet carrying value, so the two must be kept apart when net debt is built.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 30; EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9

- Governance evidence is thin: directors, officers, pay and ownership are incorporated by reference to a proxy statement that is not in the set, so Business & governance must rest on the business description, the manager agreement summary and the related-party notes.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 209; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 48

- None of the 12 documents names a rating agency, and the debt documents are described only in the issuer's own notes, so ratings triggers, security terms and covenant definitions cannot be checked against governing text.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; calculation C11
### Limitations

- The restated 2024 annual report and the first-half 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied, so restated 2024 and early-2025 values can be read only from the quarterly note and the comparatives printed in later filings.
Basis: 10-Q_2025-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 9
- No document is dated after 2026-11-04, so events between that date and the cutoff are not covered.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C2

- Management's non-GAAP measures come from issuer releases and are reconciled to income from continuing operations, but their scope shifted as Lugano and the Sterno food service business left, so period comparisons need the reconciliations and not the headline growth rates.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 100

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt of USD 1,434.11 million at 2026-09-30 is 5.61x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA and 5.11x adjusted EBITDA, down from 8.48x adjusted EBITDA at 2025-12-31, so creditors still face a high multiple that is falling because disposal proceeds repaid debt and Lugano's losses left the perimeter.

The reported EBITDA denominator of USD 255.52 million is flattered by a USD 178.00 million gain on the Sterno food service sale and depressed by a USD 57.70 million fair-value loss, which the issuer's adjusted measure of USD 280.77 million removes. Interest cover cannot be calculated for the last twelve months because nine-month cash interest is not printed; on FY2025 adjusted EBITDA it was 1.59x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C7; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C24; calculation C30
### Key findings

- Net debt fell by USD 375.20 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, from USD 1,809.30 million to USD 1,434.11 million. Carrying debt fell by USD 316.05 million to USD 1,561.27 million because USD 319.00 million of term loan was repaid from disposal proceeds, while cash rose to USD 127.17 million. The only secured debt left is the term loan of USD 233.50 million, so the unsecured notes now carry most of the capital structure.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 7–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C10

- On the house definition, total debt is 5.56x last-twelve-months adjusted EBITDA, while the issuer's covenant ratio is 4.53x against a ceiling of 5.75x. The covenant EBITDA is defined in a credit agreement that was not supplied, so the gap between the two measures is not reconciled and covenant headroom is not calculated here.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; calculation C1

- Reported EBITDA is a poor denominator in every period. The last-twelve-months figure of USD 255.52 million includes a gain of USD 178.00 million on the Sterno food service sale and a loss of USD 57.70 million on the Lugano receivable, and FY2025 reported EBITDA of USD 23.04 million includes a loss of USD 111.88 million on deconsolidating Lugano. Adjusted EBITDA is the issuer's own measure and is shown beside it, never mixed with it.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 186; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; calculation C24; calculation C31

- Cash interest is available only for full years, USD 134.12 million in FY2025. Interest expense, net was USD 73.16 million in the first nine months of 2026, USD 63.51 million lower than a year earlier, because debt was repaid and the 2025 period carried Lugano financing interest and paid-in-kind interest on the notes. FY2025 interest expense, net exceeded cash interest paid by USD 41.15 million.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 293; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation C18; calculation C23

- Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow was USD 105.17 million against an outflow in the same period of 2025, helped by a working capital inflow of USD 33.23 million. Last-twelve-months free cash flow after purchases of property and equipment is USD 124.06 million, but the 2025 comparison includes an operating outflow of USD 65.7 million at Lugano and the working capital inflow may not repeat, so the trend should not be extrapolated.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C26; calculation C25

- Liquidity is USD 180.17 million, cash of USD 127.17 million plus net revolver availability of USD 53.00 million after the Sixth Amendment cut the revolver to USD 54.00 million. The revolver and term loan mature on 2028-01-12, and the next large maturity is USD 1,029.37 million of notes in 2029, so refinancing risk is back-ended but concentrated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C19; calculation C20

- Claims outside the debt figure include lease liabilities of USD 173.05 million carried on their own lines and quarterly preferred distributions of USD 9.72 million, with the next payable on 2026-10-30, which would lift net leverage to 5.65x on reported EBITDA. The October 2026 term loan prepayment from the Lugano distribution does not change net debt because it used cash already held.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C22; calculation C27; calculation C28

- Data quality is acceptable with defined limits: FY2024 values are the restated comparatives, the original 2024 annual report is not used, the 2025 periods include Lugano and the full Sterno business, and the nine-month 2025 Adjusted EBITDA differs by USD 0.09 million between two filings. Statement identities hold in every period.

Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 226–227; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 225–226; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 188; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 103; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation C21; calculation C29
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is the issuer's own covenant ratio of 4.53x and senior secured leverage of 0.48x, which sit well inside the 5.75x and 2.50x limits and imply more headroom than the house multiple of 5.56x suggests. Sight of the credit agreement showing a covenant EBITDA that adds pro forma disposals or other items would move the view toward the issuer's figure, while a further drop in adjusted EBITDA or a failed disposal would move it the other way.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C1
### Limitations
- Cash interest paid is not printed for the interim periods, so interest cover for the last twelve months is not calculable and the interest-cover chart carries no latest-period figure.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 293; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11
- Debt is read from the issuer's notes because the credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so guarantor scope for the credit facility, floors and covenant definitions are not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; Source readiness (CP-0)
- Undrawn committed facilities at 2024-12-31 are not stated in the sources read, so the liquidity chart has no figure for that date.

## Gaps
Each line below names what is missing or unreconciled, what it restricts, its severity and the action that would close it.

- Cash interest paid is not printed for nine months 2025 or nine months 2026, so interest cover for the last twelve months is not calculable and the interest-cover chart has no latest-period figure. Severity: High. Action: obtain interim cash interest paid or the issuer's own cover calculation.

- Undrawn committed facilities at 2024-12-31 are not stated in the sources read, so the liquidity chart has no figure for that date. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the revolver commitment and drawn amount at that date.

- Several income statement and cash flow lines are presented in only some periods, or print a dash, so their cells are not supplied for the other columns; these are the other operating income line, the gains and losses on sale and deconsolidation, discontinued operations lines and the 2025 paid-in-kind and subsidiary financing flows. Severity: Low. Action: none needed beyond the notes in the tables.

- Net cash from operating and investing activities in the continuing-operations split is printed only in the annual report, so the nine-month columns carry the totals only. Severity: Low. Action: none needed.

- The credit agreement, its amendments and the note indentures were not supplied, so covenant EBITDA, guarantor scope for the credit facility, interest rate floors and the milestone fee mechanics are not established. Severity: High. Action: obtain the executed documents.

- The covenant total leverage ratio of 4.53x differs from the house total debt over adjusted EBITDA of 5.56x and the difference is not reconciled. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the covenant definition.

- Nine-month 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is 122,351 in the third-quarter 2026 report and 122,265 as the sum of three quarters in the annual report, a difference of 86 USD thousand. Severity: Low. Action: none; the later figure is used.

- Sterno food service sale proceeds are stated as about 280, about 282 and 288.991 USD million in different documents and are not reconciled here. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the closing statement.

- FY2024 and the 2025 interim periods are restated and perimeter-changed, so year-on-year comparisons are not like-for-like; the 2025 periods include Lugano and the full Sterno business. Severity: Medium. Action: use the issuer's reconciliations.

## Findings
### Bottom line
Governance and control weaknesses, not operating scale, are the main creditor concern, although fee cuts, debt-repaying asset sales and current reporting reduce the risk.

The business is a diversified owner of branded consumer and industrial companies, with 63.1% of nine-month 2026 revenue from branded consumer lines. Parent liquidity depends on cash that the eight subsidiaries upstream through intercompany loans, so subsidiary covenants matter to creditors. Board, executive and ownership detail is not established because the proxy statement is not in the sources.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 48–51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 98–99; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 209; calculation C2; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- The structure puts creditors above a holding company that owns primary stakes of 85.0% to 99.4% in its subsidiaries, with fully diluted stakes lower because management holds subsidiary options. Cash reaches the parent through intercompany loans of USD 654.94 million, so subsidiary covenant compliance is a live transmission channel: the Altor subsidiary needed waivers at 2026-09-30 and others had waivers in 2025 and 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 98; calculation C7

- Revenue is concentrated in a few names. The tactical apparel and gear subsidiary generated 30.2% of nine-month 2026 revenue, Altor 15.3% and Rimports 11.3%; Altor's three largest customers were about 16% of its 2025 net sales and Velocity Outdoor's three largest about 32% of its 2025 gross sales. Shifts at one of these names move group cash flow more than the average subsidiary.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation C1

- The 2025 restatement stemmed from the Lugano investigation, in which a subsidiary's former chief executive misrepresented transactions. The 2025 annual report carries an adverse opinion on internal control, and management said at 2026-09-30 that the control weaknesses were not fully remediated. For creditors this means reported figures carry elevated risk until remediation is shown, and the securities class action is reasonably possible with no loss range estimated.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 221; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 112

- The Manager is paid before shareholders, and the restatement showed that fees were overpaid by USD 50.4 million. The overpayment was recouped by reducing later fees, leaving a net USD 1.3 million receivable at 2026-09-30, and the ninth agreement caps the 2027 base fee at USD 30.0 million. Fees are lower, with cash paid in nine months 2026 of USD 23.3 million against USD 49.8 million a year earlier, which supports creditors but depends on the Manager's cooperation.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 94; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C5

- Shareholder payouts are limited to preferred shares. Common distributions have been suspended since 2025-05-27, and preferred distributions of USD 9.72 million a quarter continue on USD 477.83 million of preferred equity, which ranks below the debt; the preferred holders are therefore a cash call senior to common but junior to creditors.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C6; calculation C11

- Disposals have been used to repay debt: the Sterno food service sale at an enterprise value of USD 292.5 million produced about USD 282 million of proceeds, which repaid term loan debt, and the Lugano bankruptcy settlement returned USD 29.8 million in cash plus an interest valued at USD 9.5 million. The proceeds figure differs by USD 2 million between documents, which is a minor conflict. No new notes or term loans were issued in 2026, and revolver drawings of USD 94.00 million were repaid within the period.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19; EX99.1_2026-03-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_ex991sternoclosingpressrel-htm.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C13; calculation C12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a negative governance view is that creditors now hold stronger protections: the credit facility requires disposal proceeds to repay debt, caps manager fees, and lenders waived earlier defaults, while reporting is current and the management agreement is cheaper from 2027. A clean internal-control opinion for 2026, evidence that overpaid fees are fully recouped and board detail from the proxy statement would move the view toward a lower governance risk, while a new restatement, a covenant breach at the holding company or fee payments ahead of debt reduction would move it the other way.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 112
### Limitations

- Board composition, independence, executive pay and beneficial ownership of the common shares are not established, so the governance view rests on filings that describe the Manager and related-party arrangements and not on the proxy statement.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 209; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The management agreement, trust agreement and operating agreement were not supplied, so the profit allocation formula, the Manager's resignation terms and creditor consent rights are known only from the issuer's summaries.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 48–51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 113–114
- Customer concentration is disclosed for only two subsidiaries, so concentration in the other six subsidiaries is not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 73

## Findings
### Bottom line

The credit is deleveraging but still stretched: leverage sits above the covenant level due from late 2027, control weaknesses are unrepaired and most debt matures within 29 months, so creditors depend on further disposals.

The strongest support is progress already made: disposals repaid debt, manager fees are falling and liquidity covers scheduled amortisation. The weakest dimension is financial policy and governance, and the primary downside path is a miss on the 2026 earnings outlook that leaves the term loan unrepaid and the covenant steps out of reach.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C6; calculation C9; calculation C8
### Key findings

- Leverage is high but falling. Net debt was USD 1,434.11 million at 2026-09-30, which is 5.61x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA and 5.11x adjusted EBITDA, down from 8.48x adjusted EBITDA at 2025-12-31. Pro forma for the preferred distributions payable on 2026-10-30, net debt is USD 1,443.82 million and net leverage on reported EBITDA is 5.65x; the October 2026 term loan prepayment leaves net debt unchanged because it used cash already held, and the pro forma figure on adjusted EBITDA is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2

- The covenant path is the binding constraint. The issuer reports a covenant total leverage ratio of 4.53x against limits that step down from 5.75x to 5.25x on 2026-12-31, to 5.00x on 2027-06-30 and to 4.50x after 2027-09-30, so the reported gap falls from 1.22x to below zero. This is arithmetic on reported ratios and not a measure of capacity, because the covenant definitions were not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; calculation C6; calculation C12

- The headline earnings measure flatters leverage. Management's 2026 outlook of USD 330.0 million to USD 355.0 million is Subsidiary Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes corporate cost; corporate cost was USD 77.83 million in nine months 2026, so consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 189.83 million is well below the subsidiary sum of USD 267.66 million. A multiple built on the subsidiary measure understates leverage, because corporate cost is 29.1% of that measure.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 102; EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C10; calculation C11

- Cash cover after fixed claims is thin. Last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 124.06 million, less preferred distributions of USD 38.86 million a year and 2027 term loan amortisation of USD 45.00 million, leaves USD 40.20 million, and only USD 6.97 million once the nine-month working capital inflow of USD 33.23 million is removed, so deleveraging still depends on disposal proceeds.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C4

- Refinancing is back-ended but concentrated. The secured facility matures in 13.8 months and the 2029 notes of USD 1,029.37 million are 65.5% of principal, with both note series 85.1%, so a failed market window in 2028 would hit the whole structure. The term loan of USD 233.50 million must be repaid by 2026-12-31 to avoid a USD 4.00 million milestone fee, and liquidity of USD 180.17 million, of which cash is USD 127.17 million, falls USD 53.33 million short of that, so the fee is likely unless another disposal closes. Pro forma cash after the preferred distribution is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C9; calculation C7

- The business is diversified but uneven. Branded consumer lines were 63.1% of nine-month 2026 revenue and their adjusted earnings rose 27.5% in the third quarter, while industrial adjusted earnings fell 19.6% and one industrial subsidiary needed covenant waivers. Industrial weakness is the main operating risk to the earnings outlook.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; calculation C13

- Governance is the weakest dimension. The restatement stemmed from the Lugano irregularities and the control weaknesses were open at 2026-09-30, but manager fees are falling, with the 2027 base fee capped at USD 30.0 million, and an earlier overpayment of USD 50.4 million is being recouped, leaving USD 1.3 million due from the Manager. This keeps reported figures at elevated risk without changing the direction of travel.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 48–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation C13
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a more positive view is the speed of deleveraging: the issuer's own covenant ratio fell from 5.3x to 4.5x in two quarters, branded consumer earnings are growing and the interest burden has fallen with debt. Another disposal at a good multiple that repays the term loan before 2026-12-31, a clean internal-control opinion for 2026 and a refinancing of the facility ahead of its 2028 maturity would move the view up, while an industrial earnings miss, a further subsidiary covenant breach or a new restatement would move it down.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-06-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; calculation C12; calculation C11
### Limitations

- The covenant gap in the findings uses the issuer's reported ratios and stated limits, so it shows direction and not how much earnings could fall before a breach; Legal & covenants and Covenant capacity are needed for that.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 30
- Management's outlook is on a subsidiary basis that excludes corporate cost, so no forward consolidated leverage is stated and the outlook cannot be tested against the last-twelve-months multiple.
Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2
- Cash interest paid is available only for full years, so coverage conclusions for 2026 rest on interest expense and operating cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1)
- No ratings, market prices or peer data were supplied, so the profile is not benchmarked against sector peers or market-implied spreads.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)
### Company description and credit linkage

The issuer is the operating company of a listed trust that owns controlling stakes in eight middle-market subsidiaries, five branded consumer and three industrial. Cash flow is the sum of eight separate businesses upstreamed through intercompany loans, which diversifies revenue but makes parent debt service depend on subsidiary covenants and on a Manager that is paid before shareholders.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C13
### Ownership and group structure

Control is held through the Trust and the LLC, with a profit-allocation holder and a Manager sitting alongside shareholders. The senior notes are unsecured and not guaranteed by subsidiaries, while the credit facility is secured on substantially all assets including subsidiary equity, so noteholders are structurally and effectively behind the secured lenders and the subsidiaries' own creditors.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, page 28
### Revenue durability, margin resilience and cash conversion

Revenue is spread across brands and industrial products, but two subsidiaries disclose that a few customers matter, and the industrial group is the weaker earner. Margins improved with the exit of Lugano, yet reported EBITDA is distorted by disposal gains, so cash conversion is better judged on operating cash flow, which was helped in 2026 by a working capital release that may not repeat.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C4
### Market frameworks

Competitive and buyer power matter most in the consumer lines, where retail channels and tariff policy affect pricing, and supplier power matters at the subsidiary that buys moulded parts from a related shareholder. Macro and policy factors beyond tariffs do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are the growth in branded consumer earnings, lower interest cost as debt falls and a cheaper management agreement from 2027. The headwinds are industrial weakness, the 2028 facility maturity, the tightening covenant steps and the loss of earnings from disposed businesses. Over three to five years the 2029 and 2032 notes are the dominant refinancing exposure.

Basis: EX99.1_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc_exhibit991earningsreleaseq-htm.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_compass-group-diversified-holdings-llc.htm.jsonl, pages 27–30; calculation C11; calculation C8
### Downside scenario

An industrial earnings miss, with one large customer reducing volumes at a subsidiary that already needed waivers, would cut group earnings below the outlook. With the term loan unrepaid at year-end the milestone fee falls due, free cash flow after fixed claims is already thin, and leverage stays above the lower covenant steps. Management could slow capex and pursue further disposals, which would repay debt but remove earnings, so resilience looks adequate to avoid a liquidity crisis in 2027 but not to restore headroom without asset sales.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C6; calculation C7
### Overall credit view

Overall, the issuer presents an adequate but uneven business profile supported by diversification and a visible deleveraging record, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, weak governance and control, and concentrated 2028 and 2029 maturities. Cash-flow durability appears adequate, since conversion is helped by working capital that may not repeat. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on further disposal proceeds and on the covenant and earnings path through 2027. The primary downside path is an industrial earnings miss that leaves leverage above the covenant steps and the term loan unrepaid. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, the indentures and the proxy statement.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strengths are a diversified portfolio with branded consumer lines growing, a record of repaying debt from disposals that cut net debt by USD 375.20 million in nine months, liquidity of USD 180.17 million, a cheaper management agreement and the suspension of common distributions. The main weaknesses are leverage above the final covenant step, control weaknesses that are not yet repaired, maturities that concentrate in 2028 and 2029, an industrial group that is losing earnings, and a headline earnings measure that excludes corporate cost.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C3
